title: Surgical Technique for the Implantation of Tissue Engineered Vascular Grafts and Subsequent In Vivo Monitoring
protocol: Administer cyclosporine A by mouth starting 3 days before surgery.
Administer aspirin by mouth starting 3 days before surgery.
Administer coumadin by mouth starting 3 days before surgery.
Ensure the sheep has fasted 12 hr before surgery.
Sterilize all surgical supplies using a steam autoclave at 121 °C and 15 psi for 30 min.
Place Doppler flow probes in paraformaldehyde desiccator 48 hr prior to surgery.
Place ultrasonic crystals in paraformaldehyde desiccator 48 hr prior to surgery.
Place indwelling arterial catheters in paraformaldehyde desiccator 48 hr prior to surgery.
Place extension tubing in paraformaldehyde desiccator 48 hr prior to surgery.
Place Tygon Tubing in paraformaldehyde desiccator 48 hr prior to surgery.
Label each end of the probes, catheters and crystals as left and right, if applicable.
Induce sheep for anesthesia with diazepam intravenously.
Induce sheep for anesthesia with ketamine intravenously.
Perform orotracheal intubation with an 8.5-10.0 mm internal diameter cuffed endotracheal tube.
Administer inhalant anesthesia through a rebreathing circuit with a tidal volume ventilator or a pressure-regulated ventilator.
Use a precision vaporizer to administer isoflurane or sevoflurane at an appropriate amount initially (3%-4%) to reach a medium to deep surgical anesthetic stage.
Assess anesthetic depth by observing motor response to stimuli, palpebral reflex, eye position, and heart rate.
Monitor blood oxygen saturation using pulse oximetry (95%-100%).
Monitor CO2 concentration in expiratory gases using capnography (45-55 mmHg).
Maintain body temperature during the procedure using an auto regulated warming blanket (38.5-39.5 °C).
Shave wool from the entire neck of the sheep and over one cephalic vein using a #40 blade on standard clippers.
Prepare the skin of both sites for surgery using 70% isopropyl alcohol and 7.5% betadine scrub saturated gauze.
Begin with alcohol gauze to facilitate removal of skin oils.
Alternate between betadine gauze and alcohol gauze three times.
Place sheep onto the operation table in dorsal recumbency on top of a warming blanket.
Pass a medium sized orogastric tube to allow for passive expulsion of stomach contents.
Extend the sheep’s neck and use supportive cushioning as needed to maintain placement.
Perform a final aseptic scrub using 7.5% betadine soaked gauze.
Allow the final scrubbed area to sit for 5 min prior to surgery.
Administer IV fluids (Lactated Ringer’s Solution or 0.9% Saline) at 10 ml/kg/hr through an angiocath placed in the cephalic vein.
Administer Penicillin G Procaine 6,600 U/kg intramuscularly (IM).
Administer Gentamicin 1.6 mg/kg IM.
Administer Buprenorphine 0.005-0.01 mg IV or IM.
Make a ~12 cm incision lengthwise over the ventral midline neck using electro cautery.
Isolate left and right carotid arteries (~6 cm) by removing connective tissue using a blunt dissection technique.
Tie off micro-vessels branching from the carotid arteries to minimize bleeding.
Cauterize micro-vessels branching from the carotid arteries to minimize bleeding.
Utilize a non-sterile surgical nurse to assist with burrowing all wiring and tubing in the subcutaneous layer of the skin.
Use a blunted trocar, which exits through the surgically prepped incision at the dorsolateral neck.
Reach under the sterile drape and turn the head of the sheep so that the side of the neck can be visualized under the drape.
Use an 8 cm curved hemostat to tunnel through the subcutaneous space between the ventral midline neck incision and the side of the neck.
Open and close the hemostat to bluntly dissect a space for the tubing ~1.5 cm wide.
Position the tips of the hemostat halfway between the head and shoulders, approximately 10 cm caudal to the right or left ear.
Turn the hemostat so that the tips are pointing toward the superficial skin.
Make a 1.5 cm incision through the skin over the tips of the hemostat using a sterile #11 blade.
Visualize the tips of the hemostat to confirm clear exit through the skin.
Pass the Tygon tube containing all wiring and tubing through the subcutaneous tunnel.
Hold the wires and tubing above the sterile drape.
Remove outer Tygon tubing from the neck under the sterile drape, exposing implanted wiring leaving the neck.
Pull individual lines out to minimize slack in the subcutaneous space.
Leave enough distance to properly attach instrumentation to the artery.
Place 4 mm Doppler flow probes on both carotid arteries and attain an initial reading.
Administer 100 U/kg of heparin IV 30 min before clamping the artery.
Continue heparin administration at 100 U/kg/hr until the end of surgery.
Clamp the carotid artery using non-crushing vascular clamps.
Excise a portion (approximately 4 cm in length) of the carotid artery.
Suture the TEV in place using simple interrupted stitches with 7-0 proline ethalloy double armed monofilament suture.
Apply Papaverine or Nicardipine topically to prevent vasoconstriction.
Begin placing sutures approximately 1 mm apart.
Anchor four points of the TEV to the native artery by placing two opposing stitches on both proximal and distal ends.
Hold each anchor taught using hemostats.
Add 5-6 more sutures on the superficial side of both the proximal and distal ends to begin the anastomosis.
Simultaneously rotate the vascular clamps 180 degrees.
Re-establish tension on the anchoring sutures.
Add additional (5 to 6) interrupted sutures to proximal and distal ends on rotated side of the TEV.
Rotate the TEV back to its original position after securing it in place with sutures.
Remove vascular clamps one at a time, starting with the distal clamp.
Monitor for slight bleeding at anastomosis sites; if present, resolve naturally over several minutes or by placing additional sutures as needed.
Place the Doppler flow probe on the native artery proximal to blood flow entering the TEV and monitor flow rate.
Excise the contralateral carotid artery and suture it back into place if performing a "Sham" control.
Suture 1 mm ultrasonic crystals to opposing sides of the TEV.
Thread suture through the ultrasonic crystal head and stitch only to the superficial layer of the TEV.
Catheterize the artery using a modified 18 G catheter with a Teflon woven placket.
Place the catheter distal to the TEV on native arterial tissue.
Suture the placket to the arterial wall with 5/0 Ethibond to control bleeding.
Use cyclohexanone to adhere the microbore tubing to the catheter that has been flushed with saline.
Use the tubing as an extension line.
Use a 20 G Luer Stub Adapter with a Surflo Injection Plug to seal the exteriorized end of tubing.
Obtain the priming volume of the line and flush it with 10 ml of saline.
Flush the line with 5,000 U/ml of heparin sodium injection every 2-3 days.
Record the distance between the flow probe and the ultrasonic crystals.
Record the distance between the flow probe and the catheter.
Secure implanted lines and wires to nearby musculature using 2/0 Silk and a taper needle.
Position the vascular flow probe wire parallel to the vessel, with the probe caudal and the wire extending cranially.
Make a “U-Turn” of the wire toward the lateral musculature.
Secure the wire to adjacent musculature using 2-0 silk on a taper needle at two locations.
Suture the crystal wires and arterial catheter line to the lateral musculature, allowing for ~1.5 cm of slack.
Group all wires and lines together and anchor them to musculature just before exiting out through subcutaneous tunnel.

Close the surgical site with a 2-0 Vicryl suture in layers using a running suture pattern on fascia and subdermal tissue, and a running mattress stitch on the skin (fascia: non-cutting needle; skin: cutting needle).
Close the 1.5 cm incision at the dorsal neck around the exteriorized wires and lines using 2/0 Vicryl and a cutting needle.
Place flow probe wires, catheter lines, and ultrasonic crystal wires into a pouch (10 cm x 10 cm) that is securely sutured to the skin of the sheep.
Gradually wean the sheep off anesthesia and tidal volume ventilator.
Extubate the sheep when spontaneous breathing is resumed.
Remove the angiocath inserted into the cephalic vein and bandage if needed.
Bandage the neck using triple antibiotic ointment on the incisions.
Apply a Telfa pad over the treated area.
Wrap stretch roll gauze around the bandaged area.
Secure the bandages with elasticon.
Administer flunixin meglumine 2.2 mg/kg IM once during recovery.
Continue administering flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IM once a day for two days.
Inject buprenorphine 0.005-0.01 mg IV or IM twice a day for one day.
Place sheep into mobile cart to ensure proper restraint.
Acclimate sheep to the cart 2 or 3 times for 30 minutes prior to instrumentation recordings if necessary.
Remove all wires and lines from pouch.
Connect flow probe to Flowmeter.
Attach 1 mm ultrasonic crystals to TRB-USB box.
Connect catheter lines to pressure transducers.
Calibrate flow probes according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Fine tune the Sonometrics crystal measurement using an oscilloscope.
Record data using computer software.
Export recorded data for detailed analysis.
Disconnect all wires after recording.
Place disconnected wires back into pouch sutured on the neck of the sheep.
